text:
maria: Quick heads-up from the prefill run: saw a short window where a handful of prefixes ended up double-evicted across nodes. not an outage but popped p99 for some tenants.

jon: any traces / ids to start with?

maria: trace id tx-0x3b. summary: origin issued transfer -> recipient returned success -> origin demoted -> recipient failed to persist epoch before demote retry. later both sides evicted. looks like handoff ack happened before durable state.

ravi: that matches transfer RPC returning pre-persist. we should tighten the handoff contract. atomic handoff at storage layer would be ideal but heavyweight.

anne: could we do a light 2-phase transfer instead? Prepare (reserve a transfer token + persist intent) + Commit (recipient persists epoch and finalizes). prevents acks before durable write.

maria: sketched proto below. minimal and opt-in so we can roll safely. open to naming bikeshedding.

maria: ```proto
service ResidencyTransfer {
  rpc PrepareTransfer(PrepareReq) returns (PrepareResp);
  rpc CommitTransfer(CommitReq) returns (CommitResp);
}
message PrepareReq { string tenant = 1; string prefix = 2; int64 from_epoch = 3; int64 to_epoch = 4; string token = 5; }
message PrepareResp { bool ok = 1; string token = 2; }
message CommitReq { string token = 1; }
message CommitResp { bool ok = 1; }
```

jon: semantics: Prepare writes a lightweight intent record locally on recipient and returns token. Commit must only succeed after recipient has durably persisted epoch and applied in-memory state. if recipient crashes after Prepare, origin keeps owning until prepare timeout.

ravi: what timeout length do we pick? default 30s? need metrics so we can tune. also track pending-prepares cardinality to avoid metadata blowup.

maria: proposed defaults: prepare_ttl = 30s (configurable per-pool). metrics: residency.prepare_pending, residency.prepare_latency_ms, residency.commit_failures. also residency.prepare_timeouts.

anne: rebalancer interactions: if rebalancer is concurrently moving the same prefix, Prepare should validate rebalancer_epoch and return RETRY_EPOCH if mismatch. avoids conflicting moves.

jon: rollout plan: feature flag gated on canary nodes. run prefill 2h, monitor prepare_pending, commit_latency_p50/p99, and any eviction upticks.

maria: test plan: unit tests for crash-after-prepare (simulate recipient restart -> origin retains lease), integration test inject epoch mismatch to ensure prepare returns RETRY_EPOCH.

ravi: two RPCs adds latency in handoff path. optimize: allow single-RPC fast-path when nodes are co-located and storage ack latency < threshold (TransferHint header). fallback to 2-phase across hosts.

anne: agree. we'll need to be careful with idempotency: prepare tokens must be replay-safe. server should accept duplicate Prepare with same token and return ok. that simplifies rolls.

maria: migration notes: 1) enable idempotent Prepare globally; 2) roll origin nodes with small grace; 3) wait for prepare_pending==0 before enabling fast-path. will add a checklist in the RFC.

jon: add an ops helper endpoint GET /residency_debug?prefix=.. that returns {owner, epoch, pending_prepare_tokens:[...]} for manual triage.

maria: adding dashboard panels: prepare_pending, commit_latency_p50/p99, double_eviction_prevented_count, prepare_timeouts_total, prepare_retries_due_to_epoch.

evict-bot: ALERT: canary pool cp-3 eviction-rate spike at 2029-11-02T14:03Z (+380% baseline). correlating with last canary deploy.

anne: pause rollout until we absolutely validate crash-after-prepare case. jon please hold canary expansion.

ravi: i'll add tests to simulate partial failures and long-tail fsyncs. also add a simple chaos scenario that kills recipient between Prepare and Commit.

maria: owners: maria -> RFC + PR with proto & basic impl, ravi -> tests + chaos harness, jon -> canary rollout + dashboard, anne -> rollout gating and alert triage. i'll open PR today and include the curl examples for manual testing.

maria: manual test snippet: 

maria: ```bash
# Prepare
curl -X POST http://prefetch-canary/prepare -d '{"tenant":"t1","prefix":"p-7","from_epoch":7,"to_epoch":8,"token":"tkn-7"}'
# expect {"ok":true,"token":"tkn-7"}
# Commit
curl -X POST http://prefetch-canary/commit -d '{"token":"tkn-7"}'
```

jon: also add server-side metric residency.double_evict_prevented to quantify success.

maria: done. i'll include prepare_timeouts and prepare_pending gauges too.

anne: nice. one more thought: add a tiny backoff jitter when origin waits for commit to avoid thundering herd if many handoffs pile up.

ravi: good call. put cap on pending prepares per-tenant to avoid abuse. configurable.

maria: ok that's captured in the migration checklist. i'll send the RFC update and tag y'all. thanks :thumbsup:

jon: great work, thanks!
